s01 — baseline vs. iterative mapping (chr19, SNP-only)

gwct

07/31/2026 14:14 EDT

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr)
source("analyses/lib/design.r")   # bartheme(), corecol(); knit from the project root

1 Question & design

Does iterative (pseudo-it) mapping recover more true divergence than single-shot mapping, and does that depend on the variant caller? A diverged sample is simulated against the mm39 reference, mapped back, and variant-called; reference bias is the true divergence that gets lost. Iterative mapping remaps to a consensus that absorbs the recovered divergence, lowering the effective divergence each round.

Everything below is chr19, SNP-only, 30×, produced by workflow.smk (divergence recovery), het_recovery.smk (het), and read_classification.smk (read placement), all driven by config/config.yaml and launched with the run_*.sh orchestrators.

  • Truth (analyses/lib/make_truth_vcf.py): homozygous divergence SNPs at rate D ∈ {0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08, 0.10} (+ a D=0 control), genotype 1|1; heterozygous SNPs at rate H = 0.005, genotype 0|1; no indels (indel_divergence = 0, the SNP-only baseline). Alt alleles are drawn uniformly from the 3 non-reference bases, independently per site (a phylogenetic extension would instead inherit alleles down a tree).
  • Reads (mason_simulator): chr19 extracted from mm39 (samtools faidx); 30×, 150 bp paired reads, 300 bp mean fragment; NFRAG = cov × len / (2 × readlen). 3 replicate seeds — 42, 43, 44 (independent truth + reads); figures show mean ± 1 SD.
  • Mapping & iteration: bwa mem (defaults) → samtools sort/index. n_iterations = 3; iteration 1 maps to the reference (the single-shot baseline), iteration k maps to the consensus from iteration k−1. The consensus is bcftools consensus of that iteration’s homozygous SNP calls only (bcftools view -v snps -g hom) — which keeps it exactly reference-length (identity coordinates → no liftover) and free of IUPAC het codes.
  • Variant callers (an axis; each iterates independently): gatk HaplotypeCaller (reference-anchored local reassembly; run scatter-gather over 8 intervals → GenotypeGVCFs), bcftools mpileup | call (pileup), freebayes (haplotype-from-alignment). Min mapping quality 20; all output normalized identically (bcftools norm -f ref -m- --atomize).
  • Scoring: divergence recovery (cumulative) = exact consensus-vs-reference SNP diff (consensus_diff_snps.py) scored vs normalized truth with compare_vcfs.py (div_tp); het recovery and the het/other fate bands = compare_vcfs.py on the raw caller VCF (calls.norm, which carries the 0/1 genotypes) vs truth (het_tp, div_het, div_other); read placement = mason -oa truth alignment regenerated at the original seed (deterministic → identical reads) and each iteration’s BAM classified with compare_bams.py (exact / shifted / soft-clipped / mismapped / unmapped; 150 bp tolerance).
# --- divergence recovery (from the consensus-vs-reference diff) ---
d <- read_csv("analyses/s01-baseline-iterative/results/s01-base-iterative-summary.csv") %>%
  filter(divergence > 0) %>%                       # no divergence sites at D=0
  mutate(recall    = div_tp / n_truth_div,
         precision = ifelse(n_called_snp > 0, 1 - fp / n_called_snp, NA),
         caller    = factor(caller, levels = c("gatk", "bcftools", "freebayes")),
         iteration = factor(iteration))
agg <- d %>% group_by(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  summarize(recall_m = mean(recall), recall_sd = sd(recall),
            prec_m = mean(precision), prec_sd = sd(precision), .groups = "drop")
n_iter <- max(as.integer(as.character(d$iteration)))
cols   <- corecol(pal = "wilke", numcol = n_iter)

# --- het recovery + fate bands (from the raw per-iteration caller VCF) ---
het <- read_csv("analyses/s01-baseline-iterative/results/s01-base-het-recovery-by-iter.csv") %>%
  filter(divergence > 0) %>%
  mutate(caller = factor(caller, levels = c("gatk", "bcftools", "freebayes")),
         iteration = factor(iteration),
         het_recall = het_tp / n_truth_het)
hets <- het %>% group_by(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  summarize(m = mean(het_recall), s = sd(het_recall), .groups = "drop")

# --- read placement ---
rc <- read_csv("analyses/s01-baseline-iterative/results/s01-base-readclass-by-iter.csv") %>%
  filter(divergence > 0) %>%
  mutate(caller = factor(caller, levels = c("gatk", "bcftools", "freebayes")),
         iteration = factor(iteration))

# --- fate of divergent sites (cumulative-correct) ---
# Recovered comes from the CONSENSUS (d$div_tp), because a site recovered in one round is
# baked into the consensus and no longer re-called the next -- so the raw caller VCF would
# wrongly show it migrating back to "lost". The het/other bands (sites the caller calls
# 0/1 or wrong-allele, hence NOT baked into the hom consensus) come from the caller VCF;
# lost-to-reference is the remainder.
fate <- inner_join(
    d   %>% select(caller, divergence, seed, iteration, n_truth_div, rec = div_tp),
    het %>% select(caller, divergence, seed, iteration, div_het, div_other),
    by = c("caller", "divergence", "seed", "iteration")) %>%
  mutate(lost = pmax(n_truth_div - rec - div_het - div_other, 0)) %>%
  group_by(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  summarize(Recovered           = mean(rec / n_truth_div),
            `Called het`        = mean(div_het / n_truth_div),
            `Lost to reference` = mean(lost / n_truth_div),
            Other               = mean(div_other / n_truth_div), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(caller, divergence, iteration), names_to = "fate", values_to = "prop") %>%
  mutate(fate = factor(fate, levels = c("Recovered", "Called het",
                                        "Lost to reference", "Other")))

small_legend <- theme(legend.position = "bottom",
                      legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
                      legend.title = element_blank(),
                      legend.key.size = unit(0.40, "cm"))

2 Read classification

The mapping-side view: where did each read actually land relative to where it was simulated from? Each stacked bar is the composition of read placements at one iteration (exact / shifted / soft-clipped / mismapped / diff-chr / unmapped), for every caller (rows) and divergence (columns). Iteration 1 maps to the reference and so is caller-independent; later iterations map to each caller’s own consensus.

classes <- c("exact", "shifted", "clipped", "mismapped", "diff_chr", "unmapped", "missing")
class_cols <- c(exact = "#009E73", shifted = "#56B4E9", clipped = "#E69F00",
                mismapped = "#D55E00", diff_chr = "#CC79A7",
                unmapped = "#999999", missing = "#333333")
comp <- rc %>% group_by(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  summarize(across(all_of(paste0(classes, "_prop")), mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(caller, divergence, iteration), names_to = "class", values_to = "prop") %>%
  mutate(class = factor(sub("_prop", "", class), levels = classes))

ggplot(comp, aes(x = iteration, y = prop, fill = class)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.85) +
  facet_grid(caller ~ divergence) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_cols) +
  xlab("Iteration") + ylab("Fraction of reads") +
  bartheme() + small_legend

Interpretation. Read the iter1 bars across the three caller rows — they are identical: single-shot mapping is caller-independent (everyone maps to the reference), and at D=0.10 only ~57% of reads are exact, ~40% soft-clipped. That is the key control — the reads are placed the same way for every caller at iter1, yet gatk recovers far fewer SNPs (§3) — so gatk’s single-shot deficit is its reference-anchored reassembler, not a mapping/clipping artifact. From iter2 the rows separate: bcftools/freebayes recover ~all divergence at iter1, so their consensus is near-complete and reads map almost perfectly by iter2; gatk’s consensus improves gradually, so its soft-clip band shrinks gradually (~40%→10% at D=0.10). Mapping quality is downstream of caller recovery (recover → consensus → better mapping → recover more), and the soft-clipped bases are retained in the BAM and used by gatk anyway — so this is a readout of falling effective divergence, not evidence removed from the caller.

3 SNP recovery

The homozygous-divergence result — the core reference-bias question — from four angles: the fate of every divergent site, the recovered counts, recall/precision, and how the iteration benefit differs by caller.

3.1 Fate of divergent sites per iteration

Every true divergent site is homozygous-alternate and should be recovered as such; these stacked bars show what actually becomes of it at each iteration — the variant-calling analogue of the read-placement composition above. Recovered = the site is in the consensus (cumulative); Called het / Other = the raw caller VCF calls it 0/1 or with the wrong allele (so it is not baked into the hom consensus); Lost to reference = the remainder (the sample looks like the reference — reference bias itself).

fate_cols <- c("Recovered" = "#009e73", "Called het" = "#56b4e9",
               "Lost to reference" = "#d55e00", "Other" = "#999999")
ggplot(fate, aes(x = iteration, y = prop, fill = fate)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.85) +
  facet_grid(caller ~ divergence) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = fate_cols) +
  xlab("Iteration") + ylab("Proportion of true divergent sites") +
  bartheme() + small_legend

Interpretation. The orange Lost to reference band is reference bias, and it shrinks every iteration — most dramatically for gatk at high divergence (28% → 18% lost at D=0.10). The Called het band (a divergent site only partly rescued — one allele’s worth of reads surviving) stays thin throughout (~0.5%). bcftools/freebayes are almost fully green from iteration 1; gatk starts with a large lost band that iteration steadily eats into. This is the recall story below shown as a complete accounting of where every divergent site goes.

3.2 Recovered SNP counts

True divergent SNPs recovered, shown as count (% of truth, +new), by caller and divergence for each iteration (means over the 3 seeds). +new = additional true SNPs recovered vs. the previous iteration (blank for iter1, the single-shot baseline); truth = total divergent sites simulated. Rows are grouped by caller.

library(kableExtra)
fmt <- function(x) formatC(round(x), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
cells <- d %>%
  group_by(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  summarize(recovered = mean(div_tp),
            recall    = mean(div_tp / n_truth_div), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(caller, divergence, iteration) %>%
  group_by(caller, divergence) %>%
  mutate(gained = recovered - lag(recovered)) %>%   # new SNPs vs previous iteration
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(cell = ifelse(is.na(gained),
                       sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", fmt(recovered), 100 * recall),
                       sprintf("%s (%.1f%%, +%s)", fmt(recovered), 100 * recall, fmt(gained))),
         iteration = paste0("iter", iteration)) %>%
  select(caller, divergence, iteration, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = iteration, values_from = cell)

truth_col <- d %>% group_by(caller, divergence) %>%
  summarize(truth = formatC(round(mean(n_truth_div)), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
            .groups = "drop")
tab <- left_join(truth_col, cells, by = c("caller", "divergence")) %>%
  arrange(caller, divergence)

grp  <- tab %>% count(caller)
disp <- tab %>% select(-caller)
kbl <- knitr::kable(
    disp, align = "r",
    col.names = c("divergence", "truth", paste0("iter", seq_len(n_iter))),
    caption = "True divergent SNPs recovered as count (% of truth), mean over seeds.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center")
start <- 1
for (i in seq_len(nrow(grp))) {
  kbl   <- kbl %>% pack_rows(as.character(grp$caller[i]), start, start + grp$n[i] - 1)
  start <- start + grp$n[i]
}

3.3 Precision and recall

Recall (recovered / truth) and precision (of the consensus SNP set vs truth), by caller. At each divergence the grey connector spans the iterations, so its length is the iteration gain; error bars are ±1 SD over the 3 seeds.

ggplot(agg, aes(x = divergence, y = recall_m, color = iteration)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = divergence), color = "grey65", size = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = recall_m - recall_sd, ymax = recall_m + recall_sd), width = 0.0015) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~caller) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(agg$divergence)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols, name = "Iteration") +
  xlab("Simulated divergence (D)") + ylab("SNP divergence recall") +
  bartheme() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

ggplot(agg, aes(x = divergence, y = prec_m, color = iteration)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = divergence), color = "grey65", size = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = prec_m - prec_sd, ymax = prec_m + prec_sd), width = 0.0015) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~caller) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(agg$divergence)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols, name = "Iteration") +
  xlab("Simulated divergence (D)") + ylab("SNP precision (consensus vs truth)") +
  bartheme() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Interpretation. Recall rises every iteration and converges by ~3 rounds; the effect is tiny for bcftools / freebayes (already ~99% — little headroom) and large for gatk, whose single-shot recall collapses at high divergence but is substantially rescued. Error bars are <0.1 pt everywhere (aggregate recall over chr19’s millions of sites is near-deterministic — the near-zero seed variance is itself a result). Precision confirms the recall gains are not bought with false positives.

3.4 Variant caller comparison

Where iteration helps most: the recall improvement from single-shot (iter1) to the last iteration, by caller and divergence.

gain <- agg %>%
  filter(iteration %in% c("1", as.character(n_iter))) %>%
  select(caller, divergence, iteration, recall_m) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = iteration, values_from = recall_m) %>%
  mutate(gain = .data[[as.character(n_iter)]] - .data[["1"]])

ggplot(gain, aes(x = factor(divergence), y = caller, fill = gain)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("+%.1f", gain * 100)), size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f7f7", high = "#0072b2",
                      labels = scales::percent, name = "Recall gain\n(iter1 -> last)") +
  xlab("Simulated divergence (D)") + ylab(NULL) +
  bartheme() + theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())

Interpretation. The gain is inversely related to how good the caller already is, and scales with divergence: near-zero for the pileup/haplotype callers, rising to a large lift for gatk at high divergence — iteration lowers the effective divergence so gatk’s reference-anchored assembly (which fails on far-from-reference sequence) starts working again. Iteration mitigates reference bias exactly where single-shot suffers most.

4 Heterozygous site recovery

Het sites (true 0/1) are the classic allelic-dropout target of reference bias: when a het’s alt-bearing reads map poorly, the site looks homozygous-reference. They are never baked into the (haploid) consensus, so this is scored from the raw per-iteration caller VCF vs truth — het_tp / n_truth_het.

ggplot(hets, aes(x = divergence, y = m, color = iteration)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = divergence), color = "grey65", size = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = m - s, ymax = m + s), width = 0.0015) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~caller) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(hets$divergence)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols, name = "Iteration") +
  xlab("Simulated divergence (D)") + ylab("Heterozygous-site recall") +
  bartheme() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Interpretation. Het recall behaves almost exactly like the divergence recall — same caller ordering, same iteration rescue, and per caller the two nearly coincide (at D=0.10 single-shot: gatk het 69% vs div 70%; bcftools het 97% vs div 98%). So het reference bias is not a uniform evidence effect. It splits into (1) a small, caller-independent allelic-dropout tax — the pileup callers sit ~1 point below their own divergence recall (99.2% → ~97% as D rises), the genuine case where a het’s alt reads are clipped/unmapped; iteration restores it; and (2) a large, gatk-specific loss that mirrors its homozygous divergence deficit — het sites in divergent regions are missed by the same reassembly failure that loses the homozygous divergent SNPs, and recovered the same way as effective divergence falls. For the assembler, a het in a divergent window is lost for the same reason a homozygous divergent SNP is.

5 Summary

  • Iterative mapping recovers more true divergence — recall rises every iteration and converges by ~3 rounds.
  • The benefit is largest where single-shot is weakest: negligible for the pileup/ haplotype callers already near ceiling, but a large lift for gatk at high divergence (single-shot 70.4% → iterated 81.0% at D=0.10; 3 seeds, SD <0.1 pt). The fate bars show the same thing as a shrinking “lost to reference” band.
  • Heterozygous sites recover the same way: het recall closely tracks divergence recall per caller (gatk ~69%→80% at D=0.10; pileup callers ~97%→99.5%), so het reference bias is dominated by the same assembler mechanism — plus a small caller-independent allelic-dropout tax that iteration also restores.
  • This is a caller, not a mapping, effect: single-shot read placement is caller-independent (identical iter1 bars), yet gatk recovers the fewest SNPs — so its deficit is the reference-anchored assembler. As the consensus converges, reads map more exactly (gatk soft-clip 40%→10% at D=0.10), a readout of falling effective divergence that both tracks and feeds the recovery.

Scope: chr19, SNP-only, 30×. Open question: how far does iteration go — does recall plateau below 100%, and is the residual the repeat/mapping-limited floor? (Test with more iterations + a convergence diagnostic.) Indels + liftover are s02.
